title: Effort-based decision-making: A value-guided dissection and arousal-focused synthesis
title_zh: 基于努力的决策：价值引导的解剖与聚焦唤醒综合
abstract: Work often leads to better outcomes in terms of health, nutrition, and reproductive success, suggesting that work execution should be favored by natural selection. However, work also involves expending energy and time, costs that biological systems aim to limit. Indeed, work is often accompanied by the subjectively aversive experience of effort, which motivates work avoidance. Accordingly, decision-makers need to trade off the expected benefits of the goal their work aims to achieve with the anticipated effort costs before engaging in any action. While such trade-offs are relatively well-characterized, effort-based decision-making involve several other essential components, including the representation of anticipated effort and its comparison with experienced effort, which allows learning. These components and their relation to arousal received considerably less attention. To thoroughly dissect effort-based decision-making, we here synthesize the framework of value-based decision-making and expand it with work preparation, execution and recovery subprocesses. This systematizes existing research, highlights the specificities of effort-based decision-making, and identifies understudied components. Moreover, we use this framework to analyze (neuro)physiological commonalities and differences between motor and cognitive effort. Finally, we propose a novel, arousal-based model of effort suggesting that required increases in arousal give rise to effort and serve as a common currency that effort indexes and effort-based decisions aim to minimize.
abstract_zh: 工作往往能在健康、营养和繁殖成功方面取得更好的结果，这表明工作执行应被自然选择所青睐。然而，工作也需要消耗能量和时间，这些是生物系统旨在限制的成本。确实，工作常伴随着主观上令人不快的努力体验，这会促使人们避免工作。因此，决策者在采取任何行动前，需要在目标工作的预期利益与预期努力成本之间权衡。虽然这种权衡相对较为充分地描述，但基于努力的决策涉及几个其他关键组成部分，包括对预期努力的表征以及将其与体验到的努力进行比较，这使得学习成为可能。这些组成部分及其与唤醒的关系受到的关注较少。为了彻底解剖基于努力的决策，我们在此综合基于价值的决策框架，并将其扩展至工作准备、执行和恢复的子过程。这系统化了现有研究，突出了基于努力的决策的特殊性，并确定了研究不足的组成部分。此外，我们利用该框架分析运动性努力与认知性努力之间的（神经）生理相似性和差异。最后，我们提出了一个基于唤醒的新型基于努力的决策模型，认为所需的唤醒增加会产生努力，并作为一种共同货币，该货币被努力指标和基于努力的决策旨在最小化。
